**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 08:43  
[FACT] User needs to compress a LiFePo4 battery cell to meet manufacturer specifications.  
[FACT] The cell is in the shape of a rectangular cube with dimensions: 205mm height, 174mm width, and 72mm thick.  
[FACT] User wants to compress the cell on both sides of its largest face.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The largest face of the LiFePO4 battery cell has dimensions 205mm (height) x 174mm (width).  
[FACT] The cell needs to experience 300 kgf of fixturing.  
[FACT] The cell will be sandwiched between two steel compression plates.  
[FACT] Each steel plate measures 205mm x 174mm.  
[FACT] At each corner of the steel plate, there will be a grade 5 steel 1/4 threaded rod.  
[FACT] The rods run straight through the cell and connect to the opposite steel compression plate on the opposite side.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To calculate the compression force needed, the pressure on the largest face (205mm x 174mm) that the steel plates will exert needs to be determined.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Force per rod = Total force / Number of rods = 300 kgf / 4 = 75 kgf.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Force per rod (in Newtons) = 75 kgf * 9.81 N/kgf = 735.75 N.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Total force (in Newtons) = 4 * 735.75 N = 2943 N.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Area of the largest face of the cell = Height * Width = 205mm * 174mm = 35,670 mm².  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Area (in m²) = 35,670 mm² * (1 m² / 1,000,000 mm²) = 0.03567 m².  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pressure = Total force (in Newtons) / Area (in m²) = 2943 N / 0.03567 m² ≈ 82,469 Pa (Pascals).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The pressure applied to the cell is approximately 82,469 Pa.  
[USER] Asks if the calculation factors in that compression is being applied to the two faces.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The compression is applied to two faces, so the force distribution should be factored in accordingly.
